course.title: Foundations of Programming: From First Principles to Practical Mastery
course.subtitle: A Ground-Up Course for the Complete Beginner

target_audience.description: Learners with NO prior programming knowledge, coming from non-STEM fields (Humanities, Social Sciences, Law, Arts, etc.)

minimum.notes: Any computer manufactured in the last 10 years will work

install_guide.macos: Install Xcode Command Line Tools via `xcode-select --install`
install_guide.linux: Install via package manager: `sudo apt install gcc` (Debian/Ubuntu) or `sudo dnf install gcc` (Fedora)

prerequisites.knowledge: None. No prior programming experience required. Basic computer literacy (using a web browser, saving files, navigating file system) is assumed.
prerequisites.math: Basic arithmetic only (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division). No algebra, no calculus, no trigonometry required.

naming_conventions.description: snake_case means words separated by underscores like_this. PascalCase means each word capitalizes first letter LikeThis.

style_guide.braces: K&R style (opening brace on same line as statement)
style_guide.spacing: One space between keyword and parenthesis: `if (condition)` not `if(condition)`
style_guide.comments: Use // for single-line, /* */ for multi-line. Always explain WHY not WHAT.

phases.name: Foundation
phases.description: Building mental models of computation before writing code

phases.name: The C Language
phases.description: Mastering programming fundamentals through the transparent lens of C

phases.name: Data Structures & Algorithms
phases.description: Organizing data and solving problems efficiently

phases.name: The Big Picture
phases.description: Understanding the landscape — how higher-level languages and paradigms build on C

phases.name: Capstone
phases.description: Building a complete, meaningful program from scratch

passing_criteria.projects: Must compile without errors and pass basic test cases
passing_criteria.capstone: Must compile, run, and be presented with written reflection

techniques: Parsons problems (rearranging scrambled code before blank-screen coding)
section_structure: Connections to What You Know (IR connections)

subdirs.global: Diagrams used across the entire course (memory model, architecture, compilation pipeline)
subdirs.ch01: Binary, logic gates, CPU cycle, memory hierarchy
subdirs.ch02: Compiler setup, terminal basics, Hello World annotations
subdirs.ch03: Memory cabinet analogy, type sizes, variable lifetime
subdirs.ch07: Call stack, scope diagram, embassy department analogy
subdirs.ch09: Pointer addressing, pointer arithmetic, embassy address analogy
subdirs.ch10: Stack vs heap, malloc/free lifecycle, memory leak visualization
subdirs.ch12: File stream abstraction, file format comparison
subdirs.ch13: Linked list, tree, hash table, graph visuals
subdirs.ch14: Sorting comparison, search visualization, Big O chart

recommended_books.title: The C Programming Language
recommended_books.author: Kernighan & Ritchie
recommended_books.note: The definitive C reference. Read after Chapter 03.

recommended_books.title: C Programming: A Modern Approach
recommended_books.author: K. N. King
recommended_books.note: More beginner-friendly than K&R. Excellent companion.

recommended_books.title: Head First C
recommended_books.author: David Griffiths & Dawn Griffiths
recommended_books.note: Visual, brain-friendly approach. Good for struggling learners.

free_online_courses.name: Harvard CS50x
free_online_courses.note: Teaches C first. Watch the first 5 weeks alongside this course.

free_online_courses.name: Nand to Tetris
free_online_courses.note: Build a computer from scratch. The ultimate complement.
